answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The cedar multiplier is published, charged in fable, and kernel lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3864 identities would post 2348 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
